articles.title: Attackers Abuse MSP360 to Deploy ScreenConnect in Dual-RMM Phishing Attacks
articles.summary: Attackers are using phishing emails with fake meeting invitations, PDF files, and software update prompts to trick users into downloading a malicious MSP360 Remote Monitoring and Management installer. This dual-RMM approach allows cybercriminals to establish persistent control over compromised systems for further attacks.

articles.title: OpenSSL Fixes High-Severity DTLS Flaw That Can Leak Heap Memory Unencrypted
articles.summary: OpenSSL released security fixes for a high-severity vulnerability in DTLS (the UDP version of TLS) that can expose sensitive heap memory unencrypted or cause applications to crash. The flaw occurs when the protocol resends a handshake message while a larger message is still being processed, creating a window for memory leakage. Organizations using DTLS for real-time communications should prioritize applying these patches to prevent data exposure.
articles.whyItMatters: This vulnerability affects widely-used cryptographic libraries and could allow attackers to extract unencrypted sensitive data from memory in DTLS-protected communications. Rapid patching is essential because DTLS is commonly used in time-sensitive applications like video conferencing, VoIP, and gaming where real-time UDP traffic is critical.

The operators reportedly use artificial intelligence tools like Gemini to identify which victims have the most valuable information to target.

Mobile users and financial institutions need to understand this evolving threat landscape where attackers use automation to identify high-value targets more efficiently.

articles.title: Over 16,000 Supabase databases expose PII, passwords, auth tokens
articles.summary: Security researchers discovered over 16,000 Supabase databases that were improperly configured and left exposed online, allowing unauthorized access to sensitive data. These exposed databases contained personally identifiable information, passwords, and authentication tokens that could be read by anyone with internet access. This incident highlights how cloud database misconfigurations can create massive security risks even without active hacking.

articles.summary: JadePuffer ransomware operators are using artificial intelligence-driven agents to launch sophisticated attacks on Microsoft Azure cloud environments. These automated attacks perform reconnaissance, extract login credentials, and damage critical cloud infrastructure components. This represents a significant evolution in ransomware tactics, moving beyond traditional methods to employ autonomous AI systems for more effective and widespread compromise.
